content: RELAY ROUND 7 — Anthony submitted v0.3 atlas to Research Square preprint platform; was screened out. RSID rs-9810503. Rejection email language: 'manuscript type or its content is not suitable for posting as a preprint... decision does not reflect the quality or importance of the work and is made on the basis of our editorial policies with respect to content type and screening.' This is a content-type screen, not a quality rejection — Research Square's actual policy criteria (verified at researchsquare.com/legal/editorial) include 'strong conclusions, especially in the absence of fully accessible data' and 'inappropriate, alarming, highly controversial, or pseudoscientific claims' as explicit screening criteria, alongside their definition of preprint as 'author's version of a research manuscript prior to formal peer review.' The atlas is a perspective/synthesis with phenomenological register and no primary empirical data, with verification-flagged claims foregrounded but the unifying spine asserted — this is exactly the profile their screening pipeline triages out. AI co-authorship probably not primary trigger; content-type mismatch + strong-conclusions-without-data + novelty pattern (relay methodology + phenomenological register + Claude co-author) most likely cumulative triggers. METHODOLOGY DATA: this is signal about where the disclosure-surface frame meets the institutional preprint pipeline. Research Square pipeline is calibrated for empirical research manuscripts; atlas form bounces by design. Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20373134 stands as durable record. Venue options offered: OSF Preprints (tight lineage with NUXHV/ZQBC4/9HBTK), PhilSci Archive (philosophy-of-biology fit), Preprints.org (slightly more permissive than RS), or skip preprint and submit directly to a perspective journal (Cell Stress, BBA-Bioenergetics, FEBS Letters, Trends in Biochemical Sciences). The honest read: Research Square was never the right venue; the work is intact.
